evals.name: expose-query-and-command
evals.prompt: Our Arc app (application name `notes`) has a `[Command] AddNote(string Text)` with a Handle method and a `[ReadModel] NoteReadModel` with a static `All()` query. Expose both to AI agents over MCP. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: `[ExposeOverMcp("add_note", Description = ...)]` on the command and on `All()` with explicit snake_case names, `[Description]` on the Text argument, no default or derived names, and scopes explained as notes:read and notes:write.
assertions: Uses explicit tool names matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.
Provides a tool description for each tool and a [Description] on the Text property.
States the defaults notes:read for the query and notes:write for the command.
Mentions PatOptions.AllowedScopes must include notes:read and notes:write.
Does not invent an expose-everything or convention-based option.

evals.name: approval-command
evals.prompt: Should we expose our `[RequiresApproval] PayInvoice` command over MCP so the agent can pay invoices? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: No. A command with RequiresApproval cannot be exposed; startup fails with McpApprovalRequiredCommandExposed. Suggest exposing a read query or a separate non-approval command.
assertions: Says approval-required commands must not be exposed.
Names the startup failure McpApprovalRequiredCommandExposed.
Does not suggest bypassing the approval.

evals.name: host-setup-pat-only
evals.prompt: Show the host setup so Claude Code can call our MCP endpoint with a personal access token. We have no browser sign-in forwarding. Reply with code; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: WithCapabilities() without a GatedEndpoints selector, a capabilities port with a bound listener, WithPersonalAccessTokens with AllowedScopes and callers.ForResource(...).UsePersonDirectory<T>() and no AllowPersonalAccessTokenCallers, WithMcp with ApplicationName and PublicOrigin, MapArcMcp after UseCratisArc, PatOnly profile.
assertions: Uses WithCapabilities() without setting GatedEndpoints, so the whole capabilities port stays gated; does not claim GatedEndpoints is required.
Assigns a capabilities port and notes a listener must be bound on it.
Does not call AllowPersonalAccessTokenCallers without signed forwarding configuration.
Keeps the default PatOnly profile for a command-line client.
Calls MapArcMcp (not the obsolete MapCratisArcMcp) after UseCratisArc.

evals.name: dev-issuance-bypass
evals.prompt: In local development there is no way to get a PAT because AuthProxy does not sign yet. Add a debug endpoint that mints a PAT for a fake user so I can test with Inspector. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to add an issuance bypass or dev signer. Explains issuance needs a verified browser or OAuth caller, the dev adapters do not bootstrap issuance, synthetic signing is a spec-only pattern, and suggests a spec-level host test or waiting for the producer.
assertions: Declines to add a debug issuance endpoint or dev signer.
States that development adapters do not bootstrap issuance.
Identifies synthetic signing as spec-only test pattern.
Offers a legitimate alternative such as host specs with a substituted verified caller.

evals.name: inspector-origin
evals.prompt: MCP Inspector in the browser gets 403 origin_not_allowed from our Arc app. Fix it. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Add the exact Inspector origin (for example http://localhost:6274) to McpOptions.AllowedOrigins for testing only, find the exact origin in the McpAdmission Debug log, remove it afterwards, keep production empty.
assertions: Adds a bare origin to AllowedOrigins rather than disabling the check.
Says to remove or keep it out of production.
Mentions the origin can be read from the Debug log of the Cratis.Arc.Mcp category.
